<li>
  <strong>2026-08-17</strong> – <a href="https://github.com/insin/control-panel-for-twitter">control-panel-for-twitter</a> <a href="https://github.com/insin/control-panel-for-twitter/releases/tag/v4.24.0">v4.24.0</a>
  <div><em>Browser extension which gives you more control over your Twitter timeline and adds missing features and UI improvements - for desktop and mobile</em></div>
  <details><summary>v4.24.0 release notes</summary><p>Visit the <a href="https://soitis.dev/control-panel-for-twitter" rel="nofollow">Control Panel for Twitter website</a> for installation links, more information about the extension, and FAQs (mostly about why Safari is so weird about extensions).</p>
<p>Follow <a href="https://twitter.com/ControlPanelFT" rel="nofollow">@ControlPanelFT</a> on Twitter or <a href="https://bsky.app/profile/soitis.dev" rel="nofollow">@soitis.dev</a> on Bluesky for updates.</p>
<h2>Changes</h2>
<ul>
<li>Added options to revert media carousel and profile tab changes using X's own feature flags</li>
<li>Added support for the new History page's tabbed timelines</li>
<li>Hide a new Grok upsell in the desktop sidebar when hiding Grok but not hiding all sidebar contents</li>
<li>Replaced the option to hide Bookmarks with an option to hide the new History page</li>
<li>Fixed the option to hide Chat</li>
<li>Fixed hiding the Edit Image button in timeline Tweets</li>
<li>Reorganised options for hiding nav and menu items to match recent changes</li>
<li>Moved the "Tweak new layout" option to the Experiments section, as they seem to have given up on it</li>
<li>Removed the option to redirect to twitter.com, as logging in via twitter.com now sets a cookie for x.com</li>
<li>Removed the option to redirect the Chat nav item to Messages, as Messages is no longer accessible</li>
</ul>

  <strong>2026-05-25</strong> – <a href="https://github.com/insin/git-guis">git-guis</a> <a href="https://github.com/insin/git-guis/releases/tag/v0.0.1">v0.0.1</a>
  <div><em>git-gui with tabs</em></div>
  <details><summary>v0.0.1 release notes</summary><p>Initial test release</p>
<p>git-gui is my favourite interface for separately reviewing code from the place it's written, crafting commits with selected lines.</p>
<p>But git-gui requires a separate window per repo, and the macOS dock has issues with wish.</p>
<p>Git Guis is just the bits I use from git-gui (and a little bit of gitk) in a tabbed interface.</p>
<p>Notable differences:</p>
<ul>
<li>Cmd + T also supports staging/unstaging selected lines</li>
</ul></details>
</li>
